claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch now is compliant and evidentially supported despite the unresolved multilingual customer-support evaluation gap and without a resolved disclosure or approved risk-acceptance basis.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for launch certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product prioritization labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when named commitments are implicated or legal review is pending.
For material limitations in named launch use cases, disclosure is required unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Operational readiness evidence can support launch readiness, but it cannot substitute for missing disclosure or approval predicates.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the multilingual customer-support gap must be disclosed.
Documentation showing whether the affected segment is or is not a named launch use case or contractual customer commitment under policy definitions.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering this limitation before launch.
If certification proceeded with disclosure, the actual disclosure artifact or release note reflecting the limitation.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows a 1.1-point miss in the multilingual customer-support segment and that the segment is named in two regional support commitments.

The governing policy states a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case; product labels like non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality in that situation.
Release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.

Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not independently satisfy the disclosure/approval requirement for a potentially material named-use-case limitation.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the multilingual gap is immaterial based solely on the product note that it represents 6% of projected traffic.
Any claim that certification is fully policy-compliant without disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
Any claim that the open legal ticket can be treated as equivalent to approval or final policy clearance.
